_about: Rules of scripts/fgd.py check. 'accepted': deviations that are right as they are, a reason each. 'tracked': known differences that are not fixed yet; printed as warnings, do not fail. 'left_out_flags': spawnflag bits the FGD must not offer (no code reads them, or code sets them), a reason each; a bit the code tests that the FGD does not offer fails as missing_flag unless listed here or under accepted/tracked. 'flag_scopes': base classes whose spawnflag tests count only for entities that call the named method. 'left_out_keys': keys ('class.key') and choice values ('class.key=value') the FGD must not offer (they do nothing in SBO), a reason each. An entry that no longer matches a difference fails the check (stale_rule), so the lists cannot rot.

tool_keys.reason: Keys for the map compiler (ZHLT/VHLT/SDHLT), never sent to the game code. Patterns match the key name.

dispatch_keys.reason: Keys every entity takes: DispatchKeyValue (cbase.cpp) hands them to MoveWith_KeyValue (movewith.cpp) before the entity's own KeyValue (docs/MOVEWITH.md).

shared_code_classes.reason: Framework classes whose KeyValue serves every entity derived from them (delay, killtarget, master, wait, lip, distance, TriggerTarget, ...): their keys are not required on each FGD class. Keys these classes read are still valid when a class offers them.

flag_scopes.reason: A base class's spawnflag tests count for an entity only when its code calls the named method: CBaseMonster's AI (RunAI, RunTask, Look, StartMonster, ...) runs only after MonsterInit. scripted_sequence, cycler, monstermaker, env_explosion, the dead bodies, the repel spawners, the turrets, the apache, the osprey, the pitbull and the tripmine derive from CBaseMonster and never call it.

stock_assets.reason: Stock Half-Life files the editor finds in valve/ (SBO does not ship them). Names from the Half-Life FGD the file is based on; not compared with a valve/ folder by the check.

not_for_mappers.reason: 1.38 particle emitters kept for existing maps; new maps use env_particle, so the FGD does not offer them.
Half-Life source files the game does not compile (cmake/sbo_server.cmake): the class never spawns.
Ammo pickups: the FGD offers ammo_reserve; the per-weapon ammo boxes are left out until placing them is tested on 2.0.
Test builds only (src/dlls/sbo_test.cpp, docs/dev/ENTITY_TESTS.md): entities the entity tests place, not in a release build.
Created by the game code only (projectiles, effects, helpers, the player): nothing to place in a map.
Game Master mode's own entities (gmmode.cpp): created by the game while a Game Master plays, never placed in a map.
Half-Life developer and test entities, not in the Half-Life FGD either.

Second classname of a class the FGD offers under its usual name (env_spark, env_beam; trigger_random for Sven Co-op's trigger_random_time, which sets its Timed flag; the calc entities' Spirit of Half-Life 1.8 names: calc_posfroment = calc_position, calc_numfromnum = calc_ratio, calc_vecfroment = calc_subvelocity, calc_vecfrompos = calc_velocity_path, calc_vecfromvec = calc_velocity_polar).
1.38 entity kept in the code only so old custom maps still work; mappers use its 2.0 replacement (meteo_particules: env_rain / env_snow, docs/WEATHER.md).

Left out of the FGD, kept in the code so existing maps still work: Half-Life single-player level changes and saves (no use in SBO's multiplayer), cycler_sprite and cycler_weapon (env_sprite and env_model replace them) and CS's func_rain / func_snow (env_rain / env_snow do the same, docs/WEATHER.md).

teamplay_only.reason: FGD items that work only under the teamplay rules (CHalfLifeTeamplay); the SBO modes have no teams (GetTeamIndex -1, multiplay_gamerules.cpp). Kept in the FGD unchanged.

items.game_score:2: Team Points: CBasePlayer::AddPointsToTeam gives the points to the activator's teammates (PlayerRelationship GR_TEAMMATE, player.cpp)
items.game_team_master.teamindex: the team that may fire it: CGameTeamMaster::TeamMatch compares it with the activator's team (maprules.cpp)
